analysis:
The only changed file is .github/scripts/test-threat-bedrock.py, a CI test script for the threat-review tooling. The PR adds imports (Scanner, ThreatContext, SimpleNamespace) and new tests: workload-based Bedrock call policy (plan_calls, limit = planned + 1 repair slot, emergency ceiling of 500, rejection of invalid policy/ceiling/output-token configs, 600s vs 240s read timeout with single-attempt retries), two large-scan integration tests (31 and 62 source batches), and final-incomplete status-body tests that require human review and prevent clean() from clearing. The tests are offline: they use a fake native client and Backup fallback, assert no fallback calls, and use synthetic data in a temp directory. They add no production code, secrets, network calls, or runtime security surface.

The tests reinforce fail-closed properties: no unplanned paid calls, bounded spend, and an incomplete scan never clearing the merge gate. None of the provider/coordinator threat-model assets or boundaries (TB-002, TB-011, T-0xx) are touched, so no threat IDs apply. The implementation of workload policy in threat_review/bedrock.py, budget_scan.py and budget_runner.py is not in the supplied evidence. I cannot verify that the production code matches these test expectations, for example that the ceiling is enforced and that the human-review message is gated correctly. That is a coverage limit, not a finding. The patch excerpt was truncated, but the head-side changes were visible in full in the patch unit. No regressions identified.
